# Results for setup A_keep_duplicates (generated by credit_card_fraud_detection.py)

- Data file: `creditcard.csv` | rows used: 284,807 | fraud: 492 (0.1727%)
- Split: 80/20 stratified, random_state=42
- Train fraud cases: 394 | test fraud cases: 98
- Selected tree depth (5-fold CV, mean F1): 5
- Chosen threshold (validation = out-of-fold training predictions): 0.2316
- Accuracy of an 'always normal' model on the test set: 99.828%
- Train-test overlap (exact feature match): {'test_rows_with_twin': 344, 'test_fraud_with_twin': 8, 'test_normal_with_twin': 336, 'twin_label_conflicts': 0}
- Library versions: scikit-learn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3.3, numpy 2.3.5

## Automatically generated observations

- Highest AP among the three models: **SVM (RBF, C=1.0)** (AP = 0.8552).
- Highest fraud F1 at default thresholds: **Decision Tree (depth 5)** (F1 = 0.8306).
- Highest fraud recall at default thresholds: **Class-weighted Tree (depth 5)** (recall = 0.8776) with 1729 false positives.
- Tuned vs default threshold for the same tree: FP 9 -> 11, FN 22 -> 17, F1 0.8306 -> 0.8526. This comes from only 7 changed predictions (5 of them real fraud).
- On validation data F1 was 0.8329 at the default vs 0.8331 at the chosen threshold (paired per-fold gain +0.0003, standard error 0.0033). The validation evidence does NOT support preferring the tuned threshold, so the default-threshold rows are the headline result.
- Test set: 56,962 transactions, 98 fraud cases; one extra missed fraud changes recall by about 1.0 percentage points.
- Test rows with an exact feature twin in training: 344 (8 fraud, 336 normal; 0 twins with a different label).
